title: Incident Drill Scenario - windows-system-health-check.ps1
scope_note: Static analysis of a purple-team adversary emulation script. Stops at hunting hypotheses and detection guidance; detection logic authoring is downstream.
network_indicators_note: The artifact performs no outbound communication, DNS resolution, or payload download. Absence of network IoCs is a defining property of this scenario, not a collection gap.

source_artifact.masquerade_note: Benign filename and a genuine read-only health-check preamble (lines 15-95) provide cover for the intrusion tail (lines 99-153).

attack_chain.name: Defense Evasion - Execution Policy Tampering
attack_chain.summary: Sets process-scope execution policy to Unrestricted, writes machine-wide GPO-backed ExecutionPolicy=Bypass to HKLM, forces policy refresh, then sleeps 10 seconds.
attack_chain.caveat: Set-ItemProperty does not create a missing key. On hosts lacking HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\PowerShell the write throws and no registry artifact is produced. Detection must cover the failed-attempt variant.

attack_chain.name: Discovery Sweep
attack_chain.summary: Broad enumeration of accounts, groups, domain/forest, network configuration and connections, security policy, applied GPOs, scheduled tasks, services and event logs. Uses both legacy binaries and PowerShell cmdlets for overlapping objectives.
attack_chain.caveat: net groups is domain-scoped and errors on standalone hosts; the process creation still occurs. Get-ADDomain/Get-ADForest are wrapped in try/catch and fail silently without the ActiveDirectory module, but still appear in script block logs.

attack_chain.name: Persistence and Privilege Escalation
attack_chain.summary: Drops C:\Scripts\CreateUser.ps1 which idempotently creates local user 'test' and adds it to Administrators. Registers scheduled task 'Window Update Task' at root path, running as NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM at highest run level, repeating every 5 minutes for 3650 days.
attack_chain.caveat: Self-healing. Deleting the account without removing the task results in recreation within 5 minutes. In steady state the payload is a no-op, so repeated 4720/4732 events do NOT occur; the durable signal is the recurring SYSTEM-context PowerShell process creation.

attack_chain.name: Anti-Forensics - Event Log Destruction
attack_chain.summary: Clears Security via wevtutil, then Application, Security and System via Clear-EventLog. Two mechanisms used against an overlapping target set; Security is cleared twice.
attack_chain.caveat: Incomplete. Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational and Microsoft-Windows-TaskScheduler/Operational are NOT cleared and retain a full record. Clearing is self-documenting: Security EID 1102 and System EID 104 are written by the act itself.

anti_forensics_assessment.detection_impact: Rules depending solely on Security-channel event IDs (4688, 4720, 4732, 4698) will not fire in post-incident hunting after this pattern. Prefer surviving channels wherever the same behavior is observable in both.
anti_forensics_assessment.primary_pivot: Log discontinuity - hosts where PowerShell/Operational or TaskScheduler/Operational contain activity for a window in which the Security log holds no records.
anti_forensics_assessment.secondary_pivot: Event forwarding - a SIEM copy shipped before the clear is unaffected, and an on-host gap against a complete SIEM record is itself a detectable condition.

hunting_hypotheses.title: Machine-wide PowerShell execution policy override
hunting_hypotheses.hypothesis: If an adversary weakens script execution controls, then a write to HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\PowerShell\ExecutionPolicy with value Bypass or Unrestricted will originate from an interactive or script process rather than from Group Policy application.
hunting_hypotheses.note: Cover both successful writes and failed attempts where the parent key does not exist.

hunting_hypotheses.title: Anomalous policy refresh parentage
hunting_hypotheses.hypothesis: If an adversary forces immediate application of a tampered policy, then gpupdate.exe will appear with a script interpreter parent within a short window of a Policies-key write.

hunting_hypotheses.title: Discovery burst from a single parent
hunting_hypotheses.hypothesis: If an adversary performs automated reconnaissance, then a single parent process will spawn an unusually high count of distinct discovery utilities within a short interval.
hunting_hypotheses.note: Count distinct children from {net.exe, ipconfig.exe, netstat.exe, secedit.exe, gpresult.exe, whoami.exe} per parent ProcessGuid. Start the threshold at 4 or more distinct binaries and tune per environment.

hunting_hypotheses.title: Security policy and GPO export to non-standard paths
hunting_hypotheses.hypothesis: If an adversary maps defensive configuration, then secedit /export or gpresult /h will write output to a user-writable directory such as C:\Temp, C:\Users\Public or %TEMP%.

hunting_hypotheses.title: Account creation immediately followed by privileged group addition
hunting_hypotheses.hypothesis: If an adversary provisions a backdoor, then a local account creation will be followed within seconds by that same account's addition to a privileged local group, in the same process context.
hunting_hypotheses.note: Elevate severity when the acting context is SYSTEM.

hunting_hypotheses.title: Scheduled task executing a script interpreter as SYSTEM
hunting_hypotheses.hypothesis: If an adversary establishes privileged persistence, then a task will be registered whose principal is NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM at highest run level and whose action is a script interpreter with execution-policy bypass arguments.

hunting_hypotheses.title: Task name typosquatting of Microsoft components
hunting_hypotheses.hypothesis: If an adversary masquerades persistence, then the task name will closely resemble a Microsoft task name without matching one, and will be registered outside the \Microsoft\Windows\ path.
hunting_hypotheses.note: Evaluate by lexical distance against a known-good task inventory. Flag root-path tasks whose names contain Windows, Window, Update, Defender, Edge or Office.

hunting_hypotheses.title: High-frequency, long-duration task repetition
hunting_hypotheses.hypothesis: If an adversary wants resilient persistence, then the task trigger will combine a short repetition interval with a multi-year duration.
hunting_hypotheses.note: Flag interval below ~15 minutes combined with duration beyond ~365 days.

hunting_hypotheses.title: Periodic SYSTEM-context interpreter execution
hunting_hypotheses.hypothesis: If self-healing persistence is active, then a script interpreter will execute under SYSTEM at a near-constant interval with low timing variance.
hunting_hypotheses.note: Compute inter-arrival times per image and command line; flag low standard deviation across many executions. Survives log clearing and detects established persistence long after intrusion.

hunting_hypotheses.title: Event log clearing
hunting_hypotheses.hypothesis: If an adversary destroys evidence, then Security 1102 or System 104 will be generated, and wevtutil cl or Clear-EventLog will appear in process or script telemetry.
hunting_hypotheses.note: Treat multiple logs cleared within one short window as strong indication.

hunting_hypotheses.title: Read-then-clear on an identical log set
hunting_hypotheses.hypothesis: If an adversary reviews logs before destroying them, then the same log names will appear in enumeration activity and in clearing activity within the same session.

hunting_hypotheses.title: Telemetry discontinuity across channels
hunting_hypotheses.hypothesis: If an adversary clears only a subset of logs, then surviving channels will contain activity for a window in which the cleared channels hold no records.
hunting_hypotheses.note: Compare earliest Security record timestamp against activity timestamps in surviving channels for the same host.

hunting_hypotheses.title: Cleartext credentials in staged scripts
hunting_hypotheses.hypothesis: If an adversary hardcodes a credential, then a script file in a non-standard directory will contain a plaintext password adjacent to an account-creation cmdlet.

hunting_hypotheses.title: Environment-wide credential and naming reuse pivot
hunting_hypotheses.hypothesis: If this scenario reflects real operator tradecraft, then the same weak password or account naming convention may appear on other hosts.
hunting_hypotheses.note: Scoping hypothesis rather than a detection rule.

correlation_windows.note: The script completes in under two minutes including the 10-second sleep. A 30-minute full-chain window accommodates a slower human operator.

false_positives.handling: Never alert standalone. Chaining signal only.

false_positives.handling: Allowlist known audit tooling by parent and output path. Alert on unexpected output directories.

false_positives.handling: Filter on SYSTEM principal plus interpreter action plus non-standard script path.

rule_design_notes: Do not anchor on the account name 'test' alone. Pair it with ACC-003, ACC-004 or the task relationship.
Do not anchor on a hash for CreateUser.ps1. Encoding and line endings vary by PowerShell version.
Prefer surviving channels. Where a behavior is observable in both Security and PowerShell/TaskScheduler Operational, prefer the latter.
Account for the failed-registry-write variant in H-01.
Handle 4104 fragmentation: long script blocks split across records with MessageNumber and MessageTotal. Key on short distinctive substrings, not long multi-line sequences.
net groups errors on standalone hosts; process-based detection is unaffected but output-based detection would see nothing.
Task path matters as much as task name. Root-path registration is the structural anomaly; the name is the lexical one. Use both.

logging_prerequisites.requirement: Sysmon with registry, file-create and process coverage for C:\Scripts\, C:\Temp\ and the PowerShell Policies key
Command-line auditing (4688 with process command line)

logging_prerequisites.note: Disabled by default on some builds.

containment_note.remediation_order: Remove the scheduled task BEFORE the 'test' account.
containment_note.rationale: The payload recreates the account within 5 minutes of deletion. Each recreation generates a fresh 4720/4732 pair, which responders may misread as a second intrusion.
full_remediation_scope: Scheduled task 'Window Update Task' and its XML at C:\Windows\System32\Tasks\
Local account 'test' and its Administrators membership
containment_note.evidence_note: Cleared logs cannot be recovered from the host. If event forwarding was configured, the SIEM copy is the only source of pre-clear evidence.

limitations: Static analysis only; the script was not detonated. Artifact paths and event IDs derive from source review and documented Windows behavior. Lab validation recommended before production deployment.
Execution context assumed elevated. Without administrator or SYSTEM rights several stages fail and the observable artifact set is substantially smaller.
REG-001 may not exist on hosts lacking the parent key. Absence is inconclusive, not exculpatory.
REG-003 task GUID is per-host and cannot be expressed as a fixed value.
Get-ScheduledTask mapping to T1082 is approximate; ATT&CK defines no scheduled-task-discovery technique.
No network indicators and no external payload hashes exist in this scenario.
Fidelity ratings assume a typical enterprise estate. Environments with heavy automation should re-baseline low and medium indicators.

Generic names (test, C:\Scripts\, C:\Temp\) are common in legitimate use and other emulation frameworks; detections keyed on them alone will generate noise and may collide with other purple-team tooling.
